- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.16 → 81.91) are common, suggesting model fails to account for post-spike mean reversion or policy-induced volatility.
- Model underestimates late-period price increases (last 5–10 days), particularly when true values rise above 80–83.
- Forecast mean is typically 1–2 points higher than true mean, indicating a persistent upward bias.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates downward corrections.
- Forecasts show less sensitivity to recent history than true outcomes, suggesting insufficient weighting of recent data.
- When true price rises above 80, model often fails to adjust forecast upward sufficiently, underestimating the magnitude of the move.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp reversals or sudden spikes in the true price series.
